prose.kicker: Week three, from the UPS Center desk
prose.title: Bear Swept the Field; Cutting Won Two and Lost a Close One
prose.dek: Purdy outscored his projection in a losing effort, Gibbs delivered for Cutting, and a quiet quarterback day left a narrow loss on the board.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Bear Dunn swept his three opponents, while Brian Cutting won two of his three games and lost a close one to Keith Creelman.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Cutting got a huge day from Jahmyr Gibbs, but Drake Maye scored far below the opportunity he received. XFP estimates points from passes, carries and targets; it is separate from actual points.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Shawn Blake got the best individual player score of the week from Brock Purdy and still lost to Bear. Boomer, take us through the highlights.

desk.speaker: boomer
desk.text: Bear Dunn beat the whole field. Brock Purdy lit up the scoreboard for Shawn Blake, and Bear still had enough to beat him.

desk.speaker: boomer
desk.text: Jahmyr Gibbs for Brian Cutting: cuts back left, whoop, and he could go all the way! Rumblin’, bumblin’, stumblin’ through a three-touchdown day.

desk.speaker: boomer
desk.text: Keith Creelman’s defensive edge over Cutting supplied the swing in their close game; every unit’s points still counted.

desk.speaker: boomer
desk.text: Derrick Whitman started Kyle Pitts over Kenyon Sadiq. A straight tight-end swap would have changed two of his losses, with all other scores fixed.

desk.speaker: boomer
desk.text: Juwan Johnson ran past his pre-kickoff projection for Eric Martel. Eric’s closest win was over Keith Creelman, and that surprise production loomed large.

desk.speaker: boomer
desk.text: Matt Gerardi took the three biggest defeats of the week, each to a different opponent. Stu, Rich, the division desk is yours.

captions.t.offidp: Shawn Blake’s offense and defense both produced, yet Bear Dunn outscored him.
captions.t.performers: Running backs and quarterbacks crowd the top of the board; only one receiver breaks through.
captions.t.pickups: This week's top waiver-wire adds by points scored.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: The division crossover produced a sweep for Bear Dunn and another for Eric Martel, but the close games tell more of the story.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Let’s start with Bear’s side, then look at the narrow games decided elsewhere.

p.1.speaker: stuart
p.1.text: Bear Dunn swept. Matt Gerardi lost every game, and his three opponents handed him the three largest defeats of the week.

p.1.speaker: rich
p.1.text: Derrick Whitman also went winless. He started Kyle Pitts over Kenyon Sadiq; that decision cost enough points to flip two of his losses if every other score stays fixed.

p.1.speaker: stuart
p.1.text: Shawn Blake had the week’s top player performance from Brock Purdy but lost only to Bear. The week was strong for Shawn and punishing for Matt.

p.2.speaker: rich
p.2.text: Eric Martel swept his three opponents. Juwan Johnson beat his pre-kickoff projection by a wide margin and mattered especially in Eric’s closest win.

p.2.speaker: stuart
p.2.text: Brian Cutting won two of three and got a three-touchdown day from Jahmyr Gibbs. Keith Creelman beat him in the other game: Cutting led on offense and kicking, but Keith’s IDP edge was larger.

p.2.speaker: rich
p.2.text: Ryan Bousquet beat Brian Cross in a close game, lost narrowly to Cutting and then lost to Eric. Josh Martel went winless.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: The playoff board has a surprise, Rich. Brian Cutting has a losing record, yet the current forecast puts him close to Bear Dunn at the top.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Cutting has the model’s strongest remaining legal lineup. A September trade with Josh Martel moved six players and draft picks.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: We replayed the saved forecast with those players returned to their prior rosters. Cutting’s playoff and title chances rose materially with the deal. The simulator does not value future picks.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Eric Martel swept and Keith Creelman took two of three. Those results are banked, but we have not run separate what-if tests to price any one game.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Josh Martel is the other side of the trade test: his modeled playoff chance falls with the deal. Brian Cross also sits near the bottom after a different week. This controlled replay is not an observed day-to-day odds history.

captions.t.standings: Division winners take the top two seeds; every other seed goes by all-play, not record.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Now week four, Stu. Every number in this segment is as of {{f.pv.cutoff}}, and injury news will move it before kickoff -- and {{f.pv.division_games}}, so most of this week's results cross a division line.

desk.text: The biggest swing on the board is {{f.pv.g1.matchup}}. The model makes {{f.pv.g1.favorite}} a {{f.pv.g1.fav_chance}} favorite, but it is still a close game.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: And {{f.pv.g3.matchup}}, with the all-time series running the other way. {{f.pv.g3.favorite}} is a {{f.pv.g3.fav_chance}} favorite anyway. {{f.pv.g3.fav_stakes}}; {{f.pv.g3.dog_stakes}}. Upset path: {{f.pv.g3.upset_path}}. Flip factor: {{f.pv.g3.flip}}. History: {{f.pv.g3.h2h}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Division watch, Rich. {{f.pv.div.dog-pound-4-life.line}}.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: {{f.pv.div.legion-of-boom.line}}. Two teams tied at the top of that division and the model still splits them.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: {{f.pv.div.maddie-mondays.line}}. And {{f.pv.div.outlast-pg-time.line}} -- practically a coin flip at the top of that one too.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: Injury watch. {{f.pv.inj.count}} carry a tag on MFL as of the cutoff. The one that costs the most if he sits: {{f.pv.inj.top}}.

desk.speaker: stuart
desk.text: Remember, Rich -- a Doubtful tag is not an Out tag, and every number here moves before Sunday. We check how these calls did next week.

desk.speaker: rich
desk.text: That is the show. For Stu, I'm Rich, and this was UPS Center. Catch you all next week.
